Data cleaning and wrangling
```{r cleaning parent report data}
census_data<-clean_names(census_data)



#First let's get rid of the screened out people

data_clean<- census_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(status=="Submitted") %>%
  dplyr::filter(by_clicking_on_the_i_agree_button_i_certify_that_i_have_read_the_information_and_consent_form_i_voluntarily_and_freely_consent_to_participate_in_this_research_project== "I agree") %>%
  dplyr::filter(has_your_child_been_diagnosed_with_a_speech_disorder_or_a_language_delay== "No") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!internal_id %in% c(39902130, 40035826, 40034298)) #bad quality data, reporting the same language multiple times and probably asimple survey glitch where this person should have gotteh screen out for being moolingual

#Relocating the survey language column to last place (this is a new column added), so that new column placing does not affect the column select below

data_clean <- data_clean %>% 
  relocate(language, .after = last_col())

#Now let's select only the columns of data that we need

columns_drop<- c(2,3,4, 9:17, 21, 22, 25, 28, 31, 71:86, 92, 103, 114, 120, 121, 122, 128, 136, 140, 141, 143, 144, 146, 150, 151, 153, 154, 156, 160, 161, 163, 164, 166,176, 170, 171, 173, 174, 180, 181, 183:185)
             

data_clean<- data_clean %>%
  dplyr::select(-all_of(columns_drop))

#Now let's clean the column names from the very long ones to ones easy to call in the environment by using the csv file I created containing the survey expost names cleaned from R and shorter manageable names I would like for them to be called

data_clean <- data_clean %>%
  rename(!!!setNames(column_clean_names$old_names,
                     column_clean_names$new_names))


#Now let's get dates into the correct format 
data_clean$survey_date<- as.Date(data_clean$survey_date)
data_clean$child_dob <- as.Date(data_clean$child_dob)

#Let's make an age variable, calculated from the date of the survey and the date of birth
data_clean$child_age_years <- time_length(
  interval(data_clean$child_dob, data_clean$survey_date),
  unit = "years"
) %>% floor()


```

```{r recode categories to numbers}

clean_w_predictors <- clean_w_predictors %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        child_english_active_use_category,
        child_french_active_use_category,
        child_first_min_active_use_category,
        child_second_min_active_use_category,
        child_third_min_active_use_category
      ),
      ~ recode(
        .x,
        "My child does not understand or speak this language" = 0,
        "My child understands this language, but rarely speaks in it" = 1,
        "My child speaks this language mainly when someone addresses them in that language" = 2,
        "My child speaks this language spontaneously" = 3
      )
    )
  )



clean_w_predictors <- clean_w_predictors %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        caregiver_1_english_proficiency,
        caregiver_1_french_proficiency,
        caregiver_1_first_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_1_second_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_1_third_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_english_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_french_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_first_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_second_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_third_min_proficiency,
      ),
      ~ case_when(
        .x == "They do not speak this language" ~ 0,
        .x == "Very poor" ~ 1,

        .x == "Acceptable" ~ 3,
        .x == "Good" ~ 4,
        .x == "Excellent" ~ 5,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
      .names = "{.col}" 
    )
  )



clean_w_predictors <- clean_w_predictors %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        child_english_mixing,
        child_french_mixing,
        child_first_min_mixing,
        child_second_min_mixing,
        child_third_min_mixing
      ),
      ~ case_when(
        str_detect(.x, "^My child never uses other languages") ~ 1,
        str_detect(.x, "^My child mixes in a few words") ~ 2,
        str_detect(.x, "^My child speaks mainly in another language") ~ 3,
        str_detect(.x, "^My child never speaks") ~ NA_real_,

      ),
```

```{r merging new data with first collection}
## Creating a language standardizing function to be used throughout 


# ============================================================
# Standardize language names across datasets
# ============================================================

standardize_language <- function(x) {

  dplyr::case_when(
    x == "Anglais" ~ "English",
    x %in% c("Francais", "francais") ~ "French",
    x == "Berbère" ~ "Berber",
    x == "Portugais" ~ "Portuguese",
    x %in% c("Allemand", "allemand",
             "Suisse-Allemand") ~ "German",
    x %in% c("Italien", "italien") ~ "Italian",
    x %in% c("Espagnol", "espagnol") ~ "Spanish",
    x == "hungarian" ~ "Hungarian",
    x %in% c("Polonais", "polonais") ~ "Polish",

    x == "Spanish and German" ~ "German",
    x == "francaus et arabe" ~ "Arabic",
    x == "Bosnian (Serbian, Croatian)" ~ "Bosnian",
    x == "Grec" ~ "Greek",

    x %in% c(
      "Créole Reunionnais",
      "Créole reunionnais",
      "Créole réunionnais"
    ) ~ "Creole languages, n.i.e.",

    x == "créole haïtien" ~ "Haitian Creole",
    x == "le lingala" ~ "Lingala",

    x %in% c("Lsq", "LSQ") ~ "QSL",
    x == "Arménien" ~ "Armenian",
    x == "Malgache" ~ "Malagasy",
    x == "Cri" ~ "Cree",
    x == "Russe" ~ "Russian",
    x == "Arabe" ~ "Arabic",

    x %in% c("Mooré", "Moore", "Banen") ~
      "Niger-Congo languages, n.i.e.",

    x == "Non" ~ NA_character_,

    TRUE ~ x
  )
}
```

```{r making census bilingualism rate variable}

# ============================================================
# Create a Census Division-level multilingualism rate predictor
# ============================================================
#
# Goal:
# Estimate the proportion of people in each Quebec Census Division
# who report knowledge of multiple languages, using Statistics Canada
# 2021 Census data.
#
# The final variable, multilingual_rate, is:
#
#   multiple-language responses / total knowledge-of-language responses
#
# We then merge this regional rate into the survey dataset based on
# each participant's Census Division.


# 1. Retrieve Quebec Census Division names and geographic IDs
# -----------------------------------------------------------
#
# We first use cancensus to obtain the list of Quebec Census Divisions.
# We do not need a substantive Census variable at this stage, so
# v_CA21_1 is used only as a dummy vector to make the geography query.
#
# geo_uid is especially useful because it provides a stable geographic
# identifier that can later be matched to the GeoUID in the StatCan table.

qc_geo_cd <- get_census(
  dataset = "CA21",
  regions = list(PR = "24"),   # Quebec province code
  level = "CD",                # Census Division level
  vectors = "v_CA21_1"         # dummy vector; used only to retrieve geography
) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  distinct(geo_uid, region_name)


# Clean the Census Division names so that they match the region names
# already used in the survey dataset.
#
# Some cancensus region names contain additional information in
# parentheses. We remove everything from the first opening parenthesis
# onward, then remove any trailing whitespace.

qc_geo_cd <- qc_geo_cd %>%
  mutate(
    census_subdivision = str_remove(region_name, "[(].*"),
    census_subdivision = str_remove(census_subdivision, "\\s+$")
  ) %>%
  select(-region_name)


# 2. Connect to Statistics Canada Table 98-10-0216-01
# ---------------------------------------------------
#
# Table 98-10-0216-01 contains 2021 Census information on knowledge
# of languages, including separate columns for:
#
#   - total responses to knowledge of languages
#   - single-language responses
#   - multiple-language responses
#
# get_cansim_connection() is used instead of get_cansim() because
# this is a very large table. The connection allows us to filter the
# data before loading it fully into R memory.

#WARNING This line takes about 15 minutes to run unless you add a local cache space in your computer
#On October 21 the connection with the canada census server broke, before fixing, making a workarounf from the downloaded table instead of relying on the server
# knowledge_con <- get_cansim_connection(
#   "98-10-0216-01"
# )

# 2. Access the locally cached Statistics Canada table
# ---------------------------------------------------
#
# On October 21, 2026, the cansim API began returning an
# invalid JSON response, preventing get_cansim_connection()
# from working.
#
# The previously downloaded census table remains available
# locally in Parquet format.
#
# We access it directly through arrow::open_dataset(),
# bypassing the API without downloading the table again.
#
# Like get_cansim_connection(), open_dataset() creates a
# lazy Arrow dataset, allowing filtering before collect().

knowledge_con <- arrow::open_dataset(
  "C:/Users/andre/cansim_cache/cansim_98100216_parquet_eng/98100216-eng.parquet"
)






# 3. Extract the relevant Quebec Census Division rows
# ---------------------------------------------------
#
# First, rename the very long StatCan column names to shorter,
# easier-to-read variable names.
#
# Then restrict the dataset to:
#
#   - all ages combined
#   - all genders combined
#   - Census estimates expressed as counts
#   - the overall "Total - Knowledge of languages" category
#   - Quebec Census Divisions only
#
# Quebec Census Division DGUIDs begin with "2021A000324":
#   2021 = Census year
#   24   = Quebec province code
#   CD   = Census Division geography
#
# Filtering is done while the data are still stored as an Arrow query,
# which avoids loading the full Statistics Canada table into memory.

qc_cd_multilingual_rate <- knowledge_con %>%
  rename(
    age = `Age (7)`,
    gender = `Gender (3)`,
    statistics = `Statistics (3)`,
    knowledge_of_languages = `Knowledge of languages (324)`,
    total_language_responses =
      `Single and multiple responses of knowledge of languages (3):Total - Single and multiple responses of knowledge of languages[1]`,
    multiple_language_responses =
      `Single and multiple responses of knowledge of languages (3):Multiple responses of knowledge of languages[3]`
  ) %>%

  filter(
    age == "Total - Age",
    gender == "Total - Gender",
    statistics == "Count",
    knowledge_of_languages == "Total - Knowledge of languages",

    # Keep Quebec Census Divisions only
    str_starts(DGUID, "2021A000324")
  ) %>%

  select(
    GEO,
    DGUID,
    GeoUID,
    total_language_responses,
    multiple_language_responses
  ) %>%

  # Only after filtering to the small subset we need do we load
  # the data into R as a regular tibble.
  collect()


# 4. Calculate the regional multilingualism rate
# ----------------------------------------------
#
# "Multiple responses of knowledge of languages" represents people
# reporting knowledge of more than one language.
#
# Dividing that count by the total number of knowledge-of-language
# responses gives the estimated proportion of the population in
# private households who know multiple languages within each
# Census Division.
#
# The result is stored as a proportion:
#   e.g., 0.42 = approximately 42% multilingual.

qc_cd_multilingual_rate <- qc_cd_multilingual_rate %>%
  mutate(
    multilingual_rate =
      multiple_language_responses / total_language_responses
  )


# 5. Match the StatCan multilingualism estimates to our Quebec
#    Census Division lookup table
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# GeoUID in the cansim table corresponds to geo_uid from cancensus.
#
# Joining by the geographic ID is preferable to joining by region name,
# because IDs are stable and avoid problems caused by accents,
# punctuation, spelling differences, or formatting.

# 5. Match StatCan multilingualism estimates to Census Divisions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# 5. Match StatCan multilingualism estimates to Census Divisions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cd_multilingual_rate <- qc_geo_cd %>%
  left_join(
    qc_cd_multilingual_rate %>%
      transmute(
        geo_uid = as.character(GeoUID),
        multilingual_rate
      ),
    by = "geo_uid"
  )
#sanity check after the october 21st issues

# Check how many Census Divisions received a multilingualism rate
cd_multilingual_rate %>%
  summarise(
    n_regions = n(),
    n_matched = sum(!is.na(multilingual_rate)),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(multilingual_rate)),
    min_rate = min(multilingual_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate = max(multilingual_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
  )



# 6. Merge the regional multilingualism rate into the survey data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Each survey participant already has a census_subdivision variable.
# We therefore attach the Census Division-level multilingualism rate
# by matching participants to their Census Division.
#
# All participants living in the same Census Division receive the same
# regional multilingualism-rate value.

# 6. Harmonize geographic names and merge into survey data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

clean_w_predictors <- clean_w_predictors %>%

  # Remove columns from the previous join
  select(-any_of(c("multilingual_rate", "geo_uid"))) %>%

  # Standardize survey Census Division names
  mutate(
    census_subdivision = case_when(
      census_subdivision == "Les Îles-de-la-Madeleine" ~
        "Communauté maritime des Îles-de-la-Madeleine",

      census_subdivision == "Côte-de-Gaspé" ~
        "La Côte-de-Gaspé",

      TRUE ~ census_subdivision
    )
  ) %>%

  # Join using the harmonized names
  left_join(
    cd_multilingual_rate,
    by = "census_subdivision"
  )


#Code check notes: Note that there are 6 children who have missing data for census region, so of course the multilingualism rate and speaker rate below can not be calculated. All these data comes from the first collection wave, presumably becasue the question was not mandatory.
```


```{r adding density of speaker by language}

# ============================================================
# Create regional speaker rates for languages heard by children
# using 2021 Census "Knowledge of languages" data
# ============================================================


# 1. Put children's languages into long format
# ---------------------------------------------

languages_heard <- clean_w_predictors %>%
  dplyr::select(
    internal_id,
    census_subdivision,
    child_english,
    child_french,
    child_first_minority,
    child_second_minority,
    child_third_minority,
    geo_uid
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = child_english:child_third_minority,
    names_to = "language_type",
    values_to = "language"
  ) %>%
mutate(
  language = standardize_language(language)
)


# Create a list of the unique languages represented in the survey.
# This is useful for checking whether our survey labels match the
# Statistics Canada language labels.

survey_languages <- languages_heard %>%
  distinct(language) %>%
  filter(!is.na(language)) %>%
  arrange(language)



# ============================================================
# Retrieve 2021 Census "Knowledge of languages" vectors
# ============================================================

ca21_vectors <- list_census_vectors("CA21")


# v_CA21_3229 is the parent vector for:
# "Knowledge of languages for the population in private households"
#
# This is based on the 2021 Census 25% sample data and contains
# both official and non-official languages.

knowledge_language_children <- child_census_vectors(
  "v_CA21_3229",
  leaves_only = TRUE
)


# Keep only the individual language vectors.
#
# Using leaves_only = TRUE removes broad aggregate categories such as
# "Official languages", "Non-official languages", "Indigenous languages",
# etc., leaving the most specific language categories available.

language_lookup <- knowledge_language_children %>%
  select(
    vector,
    census_language = label
  )



#to avoid breaking the r memory by querying too many languages at once, I will break up the query into batches

language_vectors <- language_lookup$vector

# ============================================================
# Download the language counts for Quebec Census Divisions
# ============================================================
#
# The Census contains many language vectors, so the vectors are split
# into batches of 50 to avoid making a very large query at once.

language_vectors <- language_lookup$vector

vector_batches <- split(
  language_vectors,
  ceiling(seq_along(language_vectors) / 50)
)


language_batches <- lapply(
  vector_batches,
  function(x) {
    get_census(
      dataset = "CA21",
      regions = list(PR = "24"),
      level = "CD",
      vectors = x,
      labels = "short"
    )
  }
)

# Start with the first batch.

qc_cd_languages_wide <- language_batches[[1]]


# Add the remaining batches by matching Census Divisions on GeoUID.

if (length(language_batches) > 1) {

  for (i in 2:length(language_batches)) {

    new_cols <- setdiff(
      names(language_batches[[i]]),
      names(qc_cd_languages_wide)
    )

    qc_cd_languages_wide <- qc_cd_languages_wide %>%
      left_join(
        language_batches[[i]] %>%
          select(GeoUID, all_of(new_cols)),
        by = "GeoUID"
      )
  }
}


census_language_cd <- qc_cd_languages_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("v_CA21_"),
    names_to = "vector",
    values_to = "language_knowledge_n"
  )

census_language_cd <- census_language_cd %>%
  left_join(
    language_lookup,
    by = "vector"
  )


# ============================================================
# Retrieve denominator for language knowledge rates
# ============================================================
#
# v_CA21_3229 represents the population in private households
# covered by the Census "Knowledge of languages" measure.
#
# Using this as the denominator ensures that the language-specific
# counts and the population denominator come from the same Census
# concept and statistical universe.

cd_population_knowledge <- get_census(
  dataset = "CA21",
  regions = list(PR = "24"),
  level = "CD",
  vectors = "v_CA21_3229",
  labels = "short"
)


cd_population_knowledge <- cd_population_knowledge %>%
  select(
    GeoUID,
    knowledge_language_population = v_CA21_3229
  )



# ============================================================
# Calculate regional prevalence of knowledge of each language
# ============================================================

census_language_cd <- census_language_cd %>%
  left_join(
    cd_population_knowledge,
    by = "GeoUID"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    language_knowledge_rate =
      language_knowledge_n / knowledge_language_population,

    language_knowledge_percent =
      language_knowledge_rate * 100
  )




#Check language matches

language_crosswalk <- languages_heard %>%
  distinct(language) %>%
  filter(!is.na(language)) %>%
  rename(survey_language = language) %>%
  mutate(
    census_language = case_when(
      survey_language == "Berber" ~ "Berber languages, n.i.e.",
      survey_language == "Persian" ~ "Persian (Farsi), n.o.s.",
      survey_language == "Punjabi" ~ "Punjabi (Panjabi)",
      survey_language == "Malagasy" ~ "Malagasy, n.o.s.",
      survey_language == "QSL" ~ "Quebec Sign Language",
      survey_language == "Cree" ~ "Cree, n.o.s.",
      TRUE ~ survey_language
    ),

    exact_match =
      census_language %in% language_lookup$census_language
  )


finding_mismatches<- language_crosswalk %>%
  filter(!exact_match)



#final joins
census_lookup_final <- language_crosswalk %>%
  select(
    survey_language,
    census_language
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    census_language_cd,
    by = "census_language"
  )


data_clean_long <- languages_heard %>%
  left_join(
    census_lookup_final %>%
      select(
        survey_language,
        GeoUID,
        language_knowledge_n,
        knowledge_language_population,
        language_knowledge_rate,
        language_knowledge_percent
      ),
    by = c(
      "language" = "survey_language",
      "geo_uid" = "GeoUID"
    )
  )

data_clean_long <- data_clean_long %>%
  filter(!is.na(language)) %>%
  select(-language_type)

#Join this to our data frame to have all the predictors in place
 long_with_predictors<- clean_w_predictors %>%
   left_join(data_clean_long, by=c("internal_id", "census_subdivision", "geo_uid"))
```

```{r correlation analyses language specific}
extract_outcome_cor <- function(cor_matrix, outcome_var, language_group, outcome_label) {
  
  vals <- cor_matrix[outcome_var, , drop = TRUE]
  
  tibble(
    predictor = names(vals),
    correlation = as.numeric(vals),
    language_group = language_group,
    outcome = outcome_label
  )
}
```

```{r hirarchical linear mixed effects models}
# 1. Build base model for both outcomes

#a. Standardize predictors


model_data_long <- model_data_long %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        overall_exposure,
        child_age_years,
        speaker_rate,
        book_resources,
        book_reading,
        number_sources,
        # status_attitudes,

      ),
      ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)),
      .names = "{.col}_z"
    )
  )

#b. creating match databases so that the models are comparable 

all_predictors <- c(
  "overall_exposure_z",
  "child_age_years_z",
  "speaker_rate_z",
  "book_resources_z",
  "book_reading_z",
  "number_sources_z"
)


# Dataset for active use
active_data <- model_data_long %>%
  drop_na(
    internal_id,
    active_use,
    all_of(all_predictors)
  )

# Dataset for interlocutor matching
matching_data <- model_data_long %>%
  drop_na(
    internal_id,
    interlocutor_matching,
    all_of(all_predictors)
  )




#c. build base models
active_base <- lmer(
  active_use ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = active_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  na.action = na.omit
)

performance(active_base)

matching_base <- lmer(
  interlocutor_matching ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = matching_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  na.action = na.omit
)

performance(matching_base)

# ============================================================
# 2. add societal layer predictors and compare to base model

#a. Build the models
active_societal <- lmer(
  active_use ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
    speaker_rate_z +
    book_resources_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = active_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  na.action = na.omit
)

summary(active_societal)
#exposure and age are significant, societal factors are not

performance(active_societal)

matching_societal <- lmer(

    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
        speaker_rate_z +
    book_resources_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = matching_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  na.action = na.omit
)

summary(matching_societal)

)

# ============================================================
# MODEL-BASED INTERACTION PLOTS
# ============================================================

plot_interaction <- function(model, data, predictor, outcome,
                             x_label, y_label) {

  # Predictors included in the full interaction model
  model_predictors <- c(
    "overall_exposure_z",
    "speaker_rate_z",
    "book_resources_z",
    "book_reading_z",
    "number_sources_z",
    "child_age_years_z"
  )

  # Create prediction grids within the observed
  # range of each language group
  prediction_grid <- purrr::map_dfr(
    levels(data$language_type),
    function(group) {

      group_x <- data[[predictor]][
        data$language_type == group
      ]

      group_x <- group_x[is.finite(group_x)]

      if (length(group_x) == 0) {
        return(tibble())
      }

      grid <- tibble(
        language_type = factor(
          rep(group, 100),
          levels = levels(data$language_type)
        )
      )

      # Hold all other predictors at zero
      for (v in model_predictors) {
        grid[[v]] <- 0
      }

      # Vary only the predictor being plotted
      grid[[predictor]] <- seq(
        min(group_x),
        max(group_x),
        length.out = 100
      )

      grid
    }
  )

  # Fixed-effects design matrix
  fixed_formula <- stats::delete.response(
    terms(lme4::nobars(formula(model)))
  )

  X <- model.matrix(
    fixed_formula,
    data = prediction_grid
  )

  beta <- lme4::fixef(model)
  V <- as.matrix(vcov(model))

  # Ensure matrix columns match coefficients
  X <- X[, names(beta), drop = FALSE]
  V <- V[names(beta), names(beta), drop = FALSE]

  # Predicted values
  prediction_grid$predicted <- as.numeric(
    X %*% beta
  )

  # Approximate standard errors of fixed predictions
  prediction_grid$se <- sqrt(
    rowSums((X %*% V) * X)
  )

  # Approximate 95% confidence intervals
  prediction_grid <- prediction_grid %>%
    mutate(
      lower = predicted - 1.96 * se,
      upper = predicted + 1.96 * se
    )

  # Plot observed data and adjusted predictions
  ggplot() +

    geom_point(
      data = data,
      aes(
        x = .data[[predictor]],
        y = .data[[outcome]],
        color = language_type
      ),
      alpha = 0.25,
      size = 1.8,
      position = position_jitter(
        width = 0.05,
        height = 0
      )
    ) +

    geom_ribbon(
      data = prediction_grid,
      aes(
        x = .data[[predictor]],
        ymin = lower,
        ymax = upper,
        fill = language_type,
        group = language_type
      ),
      alpha = 0.15
    ) +

    geom_line(
      data = prediction_grid,
      aes(
        x = .data[[predictor]],
        y = predicted,
        color = language_type
      ),
      linewidth = 1.2
    ) +

    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(
        "Community" = "#8DAEE1",
        "Heritage" = "#B0DA87"
      )
    ) +

    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "Community" = "#8DAEE1",
        "Heritage" = "#B0DA87"
      )
    ) +

    labs(
      x = x_label,
      y = y_label,
      color = "Language type",
      fill = "Language type"
    ) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 13) +

    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}

# ============================================================
# EXPLORATORY INTERACTIONS: MODEL-BASED VISUALIZATIONS
# Full both-layers LMEM models
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Function to create model-based interaction plots
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot_interaction <- function(model, data, predictor, outcome,
                             x_label, y_label) {

  # All continuous predictors in the full models
  model_predictors <- c(
    "overall_exposure_z",
    "speaker_rate_z",
    "book_resources_z",
    "book_reading_z",
    "number_sources_z",
    "child_age_years_z"
  )

  # Create prediction grids separately for each language type
  # to avoid extrapolating outside each group's observed range
  prediction_grid <- purrr::map_dfr(
    levels(data$language_type),
    function(group) {

      group_x <- data[[predictor]][
        data$language_type == group
      ]

      group_x <- group_x[is.finite(group_x)]

      if (length(group_x) == 0) {
        return(tibble())
      }

      grid <- tibble(
        language_type = factor(
          rep(group, 100),
          levels = levels(data$language_type)
        )
      )

      # Hold all other continuous predictors at zero
      for (v in model_predictors) {
        grid[[v]] <- 0
      }

      # Vary only the predictor of interest
      grid[[predictor]] <- seq(
        min(group_x),
        max(group_x),
        length.out = 100
      )

      grid
    }
  )

  # Construct the fixed-effects design matrix
  fixed_formula <- stats::delete.response(
    terms(lme4::nobars(formula(model)))
  )

  X <- model.matrix(
    fixed_formula,
    data = prediction_grid
  )

  beta <- lme4::fixef(model)
  V <- as.matrix(vcov(model))

  # Match the design matrix and covariance matrix
  # to the fixed-effect coefficients
  X <- X[, names(beta), drop = FALSE]
  V <- V[names(beta), names(beta), drop = FALSE]

  # Calculate population-level predictions
  prediction_grid$predicted <- as.numeric(
    X %*% beta
  )

  # Standard errors for fixed-effect predictions
  prediction_grid$se <- sqrt(
    rowSums((X %*% V) * X)
  )

  # Approximate 95% confidence intervals
  prediction_grid <- prediction_grid %>%
    mutate(
      lower = predicted - 1.96 * se,
      upper = predicted + 1.96 * se
    )

  # Plot observed values and model predictions
  ggplot() +

    geom_point(
      data = data,
      aes(
        x = .data[[predictor]],
        y = .data[[outcome]],
        color = language_type
      ),
      alpha = 0.25,
      size = 1.8,
      position = position_jitter(
        width = 0.05,
        height = 0
      )
    ) +

    geom_ribbon(
      data = prediction_grid,
      aes(
        x = .data[[predictor]],
        ymin = lower,
        ymax = upper,
        fill = language_type,
        group = language_type
      ),
      alpha = 0.15
    ) +

    geom_line(
      data = prediction_grid,
      aes(
        x = .data[[predictor]],
        y = predicted,
        color = language_type
      ),
      linewidth = 1.2
    ) +

    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(
        "Community" = "#8DAEE1",
        "Heritage" = "#B0DA87"
      )
    ) +

    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "Community" = "#8DAEE1",
        "Heritage" = "#B0DA87"
      )
    ) +

    labs(
      x = x_label,
      y = y_label,
      color = "Language type",
      fill = "Language type"
    ) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 13) +

    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define predictors to visualize
# ------------------------------------------------------------

predictors <- tibble(
  predictor = c(
    "overall_exposure_z",
    "speaker_rate_z",
    "book_resources_z",
    "book_reading_z",
    "number_sources_z"
  ),
  label = c(
    "Overall language exposure (z)",
    "Speaker rate (z)",
    "Access to books (z)",
    "Book reading (z)",
    "Number of language sources (z)"
  ),
  title = c(
    "Exposure",
    "Speaker rate",
    "Book resources",
    "Reading",
    "Sources"
  )
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Generate plots using fitted LMEMs
# ------------------------------------------------------------

active_plots <- purrr::map2(
  predictors$predictor,
  predictors$label,
  ~ plot_interaction(
    model = active_interaction,
    data = active_int_data,
    predictor = .x,
    outcome = "active_use",
    x_label = .y,
    y_label = "Active language use"
  )
)

matching_plots <- purrr::map2(
  predictors$predictor,
  predictors$label,
  ~ plot_interaction(
    model = matching_interaction,
    data = matching_int_data,
    predictor = .x,
    outcome = "interlocutor_matching",
    x_label = .y,
    y_label = "Interlocutor matching (%)"
  )
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Apply titles and formatting
# ------------------------------------------------------------

larger_theme <- theme(
  plot.title = element_text(
    size = 15,
    face = "bold",
    margin = margin(b = 8)
  ),
  axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
  axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
  legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
  plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 8, 8)
)

all_plots <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(predictors))) {

  active_plots[[i]] <- active_plots[[i]] +
    labs(
      title = paste0(
        LETTERS[2 * i - 1], ". ",
        predictors$title[i],
        " × Language type"
      )
    ) +
    larger_theme

  matching_plots[[i]] <- matching_plots[[i]] +
    labs(
      title = paste0(
        LETTERS[2 * i], ". ",
        predictors$title[i],
        " × Language type"
      )
    ) +
    larger_theme

  all_plots <- append(
    all_plots,
    list(active_plots[[i]], matching_plots[[i]])
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Combine plots: 2 columns x 5 rows
# ------------------------------------------------------------

interaction_figure <- wrap_plots(
  all_plots,
  ncol = 2,
  guides = "collect"
) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

interaction_figure

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Save high-resolution figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  "exploratory_language_interactions_adjusted.png",
  interaction_figure,
  width = 10,
  height = 20,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```

```{r logistic models}
  1 - as.numeric(
    logLik(model) / logLik(update(model, . ~ 1))
  )
}

# Function to extract likelihood-ratio comparisons
extract_lr <- function(model_small, model_large,
                       outcome, comparison) {

  result <- anova(
    model_small,
    model_large,
    test = "Chisq"
  )

  tibble(
    Outcome = outcome,
    Comparison = comparison,
    Chi_square = result$Deviance[2],
    df = result$Df[2],
    p = result$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]
  )
}

anova_log_table <- bind_rows(
  extract_lr(
    active_societal_log,
    active_both_log,
    "Degree of activeness",
    "Societal vs. both"
  ),
  extract_lr(
    active_family_log,
    active_both_log,
    "Degree of activeness",
    "Family vs. both"
  ),
  extract_lr(
    matching_societal_log,
    matching_both_log,
    "Language matching",
    "Societal vs. both"
  ),
  extract_lr(
    matching_family_log,
    matching_both_log,
    "Language matching",
    "Family vs. both"
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    Chi_square = round(Chi_square, 2),
    p = ifelse(
      p < .001,
      "< .001",
      sprintf("%.3f", p)
    )
  )

anova_log_flex <- flextable(anova_log_table) |>
  set_header_labels(
    Chi_square = "χ²",
    df = "df",
    p = "p"
  ) |>
  theme_booktabs() |>
  autofit()

anova_log_flex
```

```{r fixed exploratory}
#

# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(lme4)
library(broom.mixed)


# ============================================================
# 1. DEFINE THRESHOLDS
# ============================================================

ACTIVE_THRESHOLD <- 2
MATCHING_THRESHOLD <- 50


# ============================================================
# 2. CLASSIFY CHILDREN INTO LANGUAGE GROUPS
# ============================================================
# Use the cleaned language-level dataset.
# This avoids counting "Non" or empty language slots.

language_groups <- model_data_long %>%
  distinct(internal_id, language, language_type) %>%
  group_by(internal_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_languages = n(),
    n_community = sum(language_type == "Community"),
    n_heritage = sum(language_type == "Heritage"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    language_group = case_when(
      n_languages >= 3 ~ "Trilinguals+",

      n_languages == 2 & n_community == 2 ~
        "Community bilinguals",

      n_languages == 2 &
        n_community == 1 &
        n_heritage == 1 ~
        "Community–Heritage bilinguals",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    language_group = factor(
      language_group,
      levels = c(
        "Community bilinguals",
        "Community–Heritage bilinguals",
        "Trilinguals+"
      )
    )
  )

# Check group sizes
print(language_groups %>% count(language_group))

# Verify no missing classifications or duplicate IDs
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(language_groups$language_group),
  !anyDuplicated(language_groups$internal_id),
  nrow(language_groups) ==
    n_distinct(model_data_long$internal_id)
)

# Verify previously misclassified child
stopifnot(
  as.character(
    language_groups$language_group[
      language_groups$internal_id == 39976965
    ]
  ) == "Community–Heritage bilinguals"
)


# ============================================================
# 3. PREPARE LANGUAGE-LEVEL THRESHOLD DATA
# ============================================================

threshold_plot_data <- model_data_long %>%
  left_join(
    language_groups %>%
      select(internal_id, language_group),
    by = "internal_id",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    language_type = factor(
      as.character(language_type),
      levels = c("Community", "Heritage")
    ),

    below_activeness = case_when(
      is.na(active_use) ~ NA_integer_,
      active_use < ACTIVE_THRESHOLD ~ 1L,
      TRUE ~ 0L
    ),

    below_matching = case_when(
      is.na(interlocutor_matching) ~ NA_integer_,
      interlocutor_matching < MATCHING_THRESHOLD ~ 1L,

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Exact paired comparison function
# ------------------------------------------------------------

run_paired_test <- function(data, outcome_name) {

  dat <- data %>%
    filter(outcome_metric == outcome_name)

  paired_table <- table(
    Community = factor(dat$Community, levels = c(0, 1)),
    Heritage = factor(dat$Heritage, levels = c(0, 1))
  )

  cat("\n====================================\n")
  cat("PAIRED TEST:", outcome_name, "\n")
  cat("====================================\n")

  print(paired_table)

  # Heritage below, Community above
  b <- sum(
    dat$Community == 0 &
      dat$Heritage == 1
  )

  # Community below, Heritage above
  c <- sum(
    dat$Community == 1 &
      dat$Heritage == 0
  )

  if (b + c > 0) {
    result <- binom.test(
      x = b,
      n = b + c,
      p = 0.5
    )
    p_value <- result$p.value
  } else {
    p_value <- 1
  }

  tibble(
    Outcome = outcome_name,
    N_children = nrow(dat),
    Heritage_below_Community_above = b,
    Community_below_Heritage_above = c,
    Discordant_pairs = b + c,
    p_value = p_value
  )
}

bilingual_results <- purrr::map_dfr(
  c("Active language use", "Interlocutor matching"),
  ~ run_paired_test(bilingual_paired, .x)
)

print(bilingual_results)

# BINOMIAL MIXED-EFFECTS MODELS

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Function: GLMM by outcome
# ------------------------------------------------------------

run_trilingual_model <- function(data, outcome_name) {

  dat <- data %>%
    filter(outcome_metric == outcome_name) %>%
    droplevels()

  cat("\n====================================\n")
  cat("TRILINGUAL MODEL:", outcome_name, "\n")
  cat("====================================\n")

  cat("Observations:", nrow(dat), "\n")
  cat("Children:", n_distinct(dat$internal_id), "\n")

  null_model <- glmer(
    below_threshold ~ 1 + (1 | internal_id),
    data = dat,
    family = binomial,
    control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )

  language_model <- glmer(
    below_threshold ~ language_type + (1 | internal_id),
    data = dat,
    family = binomial,
    control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )

  comparison <- anova(
    null_model,
    language_model,
    test = "Chisq"
  )

  odds_ratios <- broom.mixed::tidy(
    language_model,
    effects = "fixed",
    conf.int = TRUE,
    conf.method = "Wald",
    exponentiate = TRUE
  )

  singular <- lme4::isSingular(language_model)

  convergence_messages <-
    language_model@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages

  cat("\nMODEL COMPARISON\n")
  print(comparison)

  cat("\nMODEL COEFFICIENTS\n")
  print(summary(language_model))

  cat("\nODDS RATIOS\n")
  print(odds_ratios)

  cat("\nMODEL DIAGNOSTICS\n")
  cat("Singular:", singular, "\n")

  if (length(convergence_messages) > 0) {
    print(convergence_messages)
  } else {
    cat("No convergence warnings.\n")
  }

  print(VarCorr(language_model))

  list(
    null_model = null_model,
    language_model = language_model,
    comparison = comparison,
    odds_ratios = odds_ratios,
    singular = singular,
    convergence_messages = convergence_messages
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 10. RUN TRILINGUAL MODELS
# ============================================================

trilingual_active <- run_trilingual_model(
  trilingual_data,
  "Active language use"
)

trilingual_matching <- run_trilingual_model(
  trilingual_data,
  "Interlocutor matching"
)


# ============================================================
# 11. EXTRACT RESULTS FOR REPORTING
# ============================================================

trilingual_results <- bind_rows(
  trilingual_active$odds_ratios %>%
    mutate(Outcome = "Active language use"),

  trilingual_matching$odds_ratios %>%
    mutate(Outcome = "Interlocutor matching")
) %>%
  filter(term == "language_typeHeritage") %>%
  select(
    Outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high,
    p.value
  )

cat("\n====================================\n")
cat("FINAL PAIRED COMPARISONS\n")
cat("====================================\n")
print(bilingual_results)

cat("\n====================================\n")
cat("FINAL TRILINGUAL ODDS RATIOS\n")
cat("====================================\n")
print(trilingual_results)


# ============================================================
# 12. FINAL AUDIT CHECKS
# ============================================================

# Confirm groups agree with the source classification
classification_check <- threshold_plot_data %>%
  distinct(internal_id, language_group) %>%
  left_join(
    language_groups %>%
      select(
        internal_id,
        current_group = language_group
      ),
    by = "internal_id"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    as.character(language_group) !=
      as.character(current_group) |
      is.na(current_group)
  )

stopifnot(nrow(classification_check) == 0)

# Confirm number of children and observations
final_sample_check <- threshold_test_data %>%
  group_by(outcome_metric, language_group) %>%
  summarise(
    N_children = n_distinct(internal_id),
    N_languages = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(final_sample_check)

cat("\n====================================\n")
cat("EXPLORATORY ANALYSIS AUDIT COMPLETED\n")
cat("====================================\n")
cat("No duplicate child-language-outcome rows.\n")
cat("Language classifications are consistent.\n")
cat("Figure and statistical test summaries agree.\n")
cat("Check GLMM singularity and warnings above.\n")




# ============================================================
# SENSITIVITY: Singular trilingual active-use GLMM
# Logistic regression with child-cluster-robust SEs
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

tri_active_data <- trilingual_data %>%
  filter(outcome_metric == "Active language use") %>%
  droplevels()

# Fit ordinary logistic regression
tri_active_glm <- glm(
  below_threshold ~ language_type,
  data = tri_active_data,
  family = binomial
)

# Cluster-robust covariance matrix
cluster_vcov <- sandwich::vcovCL(
  tri_active_glm,
  cluster = tri_active_data$internal_id,
  type = "HC1"
)

# Cluster-robust coefficient tests
lmtest::coeftest(
  tri_active_glm,
  vcov. = cluster_vcov,
  df = n_distinct(tri_active_data$internal_id) - 1
)

# Odds ratio and cluster-robust 95% CI
estimate <- coef(tri_active_glm)["language_typeHeritage"]

robust_se <- sqrt(
  diag(cluster_vcov)
)["language_typeHeritage"]

critical_value <- qt(
  0.975,
  df = n_distinct(tri_active_data$internal_id) - 1
)

data.frame(
  predictor = "Heritage vs Community",
  OR = exp(estimate),
  CI_lower = exp(
    estimate - critical_value * robust_se
  ),
  CI_upper = exp(
    estimate + critical_value * robust_se
  )
)
```

```{r methods descriptives}
#---------------------------------------------
#LANGUAGE COMBINATION
#--------------------------------------------

# 1. IDENTIFY EACH CHILD'S LANGUAGE COMBINATION


language_composition <- model_data_long %>%
  
  # One row per child-language
  distinct(internal_id, language, language_type) %>%
  
  group_by(internal_id) %>%
  
  summarise(
    n_languages = n_distinct(language),
    
    n_english = sum(language_type == "English"),
    n_french = sum(language_type == "French"),
    n_minority = sum(language_type == "Minority"),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # Broad number-of-languages category
  mutate(
    multilingual_group = case_when(
      n_languages == 1 ~ "Monolingual",
      n_languages == 2 ~ "Bilingual",
      n_languages == 3 ~ "Trilingual",
      n_languages >= 4 ~ "4+ languages"
    ),
    
    # Composition within each category
    language_combination = case_when(
      
      # -----------------------
      # Monolingual
      # -----------------------
      n_languages == 1 & n_english == 1 ~ "English",
      n_languages == 1 & n_french == 1 ~ "French",
      n_languages == 1 & n_minority == 1 ~ "Minority",
      
      
      # -----------------------
      # Bilingual
      # -----------------------
      n_languages == 2 &
        n_english == 1 & n_french == 1 ~
        "English + French",
      
      n_languages == 2 &
        n_english == 1 & n_minority == 1 ~
        "English + Minority",
      
      n_languages == 2 &
        n_french == 1 & n_minority == 1 ~
        "French + Minority",
      
      n_languages == 2 &
        n_minority == 2 ~
        "Minority + Minority",
      
      
      # -----------------------
      # Trilingual
      # -----------------------
      n_languages == 3 &
        n_english == 1 &
        n_french == 1 &
        n_minority == 1 ~
        "English + French + Minority",
      
      n_languages == 3 &
        n_english == 1 &
        n_minority == 2 ~
        "English + 2 Minority",
      
      n_languages == 3 &
        n_french == 1 &
        n_minority == 2 ~
        "French + 2 Minority",
      
      n_languages == 3 &
        n_minority == 3 ~
        "3 Minority",
      
      
      # -----------------------
      # 4+
      # -----------------------
      n_languages >= 4 ~ "4+ languages",
      
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )



language_composition %>%
  count(
    multilingual_group,
    language_combination
  )


# ============================================================
# 2. CREATE STACKED-BAR DATA
# ============================================================

language_composition_summary <- language_composition %>%
  count(
    multilingual_group,
    language_combination,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%
  group_by(multilingual_group) %>%
  mutate(
    group_total = sum(n),
    percent_within_group = n / group_total * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    total_sample = sum(n),
    group_percent = group_total / total_sample * 100,
    
    multilingual_group = factor(
      multilingual_group,
      levels = c(
        "Monolingual",
        "Bilingual",
        "Trilingual",
        "4+ languages"
      )
    )
  )
  


# ============================================================
# 3. STACKED LANGUAGE-COMBINATION GRAPH
# ============================================================

# Set explicit order for bars
language_composition_summary <- language_composition_summary %>%
  mutate(
    multilingual_group = factor(
      multilingual_group,
      levels = c(
        "Bilingual",
        "Trilingual",
        "4+ languages"
      )
    ),
    
    # Explicit order for slices AND legend
    language_combination = factor(
      language_combination,
      levels = c(
        # Bilingual
        "English + French",
        "French + Minority",
        "English + Minority",
        "Minority + Minority",
        
        # Trilingual
        "English + French + Minority",
        "French + 2 Minority",
        "English + 2 Minority",
        "3 Minority",
        
        # 4+
        "4+ languages"
      )
    )
  )


ggplot(
  language_composition_summary,
  aes(
    x = multilingual_group,
    y = n,
    fill = language_combination
  )
) +
  
  geom_col(
    width = 0.7,
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  
  # Percentage of entire sample above each bar
  geom_text(
    data = language_composition_summary %>%
      distinct(
        multilingual_group,
        group_total,
        group_percent
      ),
    aes(
      x = multilingual_group,
      y = group_total,
      label = paste0(
        round(group_percent, 1),
        "%"
      )
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 20 / ggplot2::.pt
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      # -------------------------
      # Bilingual combinations
      # -------------------------
      "English + French" = "#B0DA87",
      "French + Minority" = "#8DAEE1",
      "English + Minority" = "#FAE0BD",
      "Minority + Minority" = "#C6A7D8",
      
      # -------------------------
      # Trilingual combinations
      # -------------------------
      "English + French + Minority" = "#69B3A2",
      "French + 2 Minority" = "#7896CC",

      "3 Minority" = "#9A77B5",
```

```{r predictors tables methods}
      )
    })
  ) %>%
  filter(!available)



summarise_predictor <- function(data, variable) {

  x <- data[[variable]]

  if (!is.numeric(x)) {
    stop("Variable is not numeric: ", variable)
  }

  x <- x[is.finite(x)]

  tibble(
    N = length(x),
    Mean = if (length(x)) mean(x) else NA_real_,
    SD = if (length(x) > 1) sd(x) else NA_real_,
    Median = if (length(x)) median(x) else NA_real_,
    Minimum = if (length(x)) min(x) else NA_real_,
    Maximum = if (length(x)) max(x) else NA_real_
  )
}


# ============================================================
# Create descriptive statistics for all predictors
# using the updated predictor dictionary
# ============================================================

make_predictor_summary <- function(
    dictionary,
    child_data,
    language_data
) {

  results <- vector("list", nrow(dictionary))

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(dictionary))) {

    # Extract information from dictionary
    v <- dictionary$variable[i]
    analysis <- dictionary$analyses_level[i]

    # Select dataset based on analysis level
    if (analysis %in% c("Both", "Language agnostic")) {

      dat <- child_data

    } else if (analysis == "Language specific") {

      dat <- language_data

    } else {

      stop(
        "Unknown analyses_level for variable ",
        v, ": ", analysis
      )
    }

    # Check that variable exists in selected dataset
    if (!v %in% names(dat)) {
      stop(
        "Variable '", v,
        "' not found in dataset for ",
        analysis
      )
    }

    # Calculate descriptive statistics
    results[[i]] <- dplyr::bind_cols(
      dictionary[i, ],
      summarise_predictor(dat, v)
    )
  }

  # Combine all predictor summaries
  dplyr::bind_rows(results)
}

# ============================================================
# Generate overall descriptive statistics
# ============================================================

  child_data = child_data,

format_predictor_table <- function(summary_data) {

  summary_data %>%
    mutate(
      `M (SD)` = if_else(
        is.na(SD),
        sprintf("%.2f (—)", Mean),
        sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", Mean, SD)
      ),
      Median = sprintf("%.2f", Median),
      Range = sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", Minimum, Maximum)
    ) %>%
    select(
      Layer = layer,
      Predictor = label,
      `Analysis level` = analyses_level,
      N,
      `M (SD)`,
      Median,
      Range
    )
}
```

```{r code audit, model diagnostics}
# AUDIT: Main mixed-effects model diagnostics

library(lme4)

models_to_check <- list(
  active_societal = active_societal,
  active_family = active_family,

  matching_family = matching_family,

)



# ============================================================
# AUDIT: Model convergence and singularity
# ============================================================

diagnostic_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  models_to_check,
  function(fit, model_name) {

    conv_messages <- fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages

    tibble::tibble(
      model_name = model_name,
      n_obs = stats::nobs(fit),
      singular = lme4::isSingular(fit),
      convergence_warning = if (length(conv_messages) == 0) {
        "None"
      } else {
        paste(conv_messages, collapse = "; ")
      },
      residual_sd = stats::sigma(fit)
    )
  }
)

#Because some of the gaussian assumptions are violated, running a bootstrap analysis (sensitivity analyses) to see if the results we found for the LMEM are still significant 


# ============================================================
# SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS: Participant-cluster bootstrap
# 500 replicates for each selected mixed-effects model
# ============================================================

library(lme4)

cluster_bootstrap <- function(fit, B = 500, seed = 123) {

  set.seed(seed)

  # Use exactly the observations used in the fitted model
  dat <- model.frame(fit)
  original_beta <- lme4::fixef(fit)
  terms <- names(original_beta)

  # Store each child's rows together
  child_rows <- split(
    seq_len(nrow(dat)),
    as.character(dat$internal_id)
  )

  child_ids <- names(child_rows)
  n_children <- length(child_ids)

  # Storage
  boot_coefs <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = B,
    ncol = length(terms),
    dimnames = list(NULL, terms)
  )

  failed <- logical(B)
  singular <- logical(B)
  convergence <- logical(B)

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {

    # Sample children with replacement
    sampled <- sample(
      child_ids,
      size = n_children,
      replace = TRUE
    )

    # Include every language row for each sampled child.
    # Assign a NEW cluster ID to each sampled copy.
    boot_dat <- do.call(
      rbind,
      lapply(seq_along(sampled), function(i) {

        child_dat <- dat[
          child_rows[[sampled[i]]],
          ,
          drop = FALSE
        ]

        child_dat$internal_id <- paste0("boot_", i)

        child_dat
      })
    )

    boot_dat$internal_id <- factor(
      boot_dat$internal_id
    )

    # Refit the same model specification
    boot_fit <- tryCatch(
      suppressWarnings(
        lme4::lmer(
          formula(fit),
          data = boot_dat,
          REML = FALSE,
          control = lme4::lmerControl(
            optimizer = "bobyqa",
            optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000)
          )
        )
      ),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )

    if (is.null(boot_fit)) {
      failed[b] <- TRUE
      next
    }

    beta <- lme4::fixef(boot_fit)

    # Record any unidentified/rank-deficient coefficients
    if (!all(terms %in% names(beta))) {
      failed[b] <- TRUE
      next
    }

    boot_coefs[b, ] <- beta[terms]

    singular[b] <- lme4::isSingular(boot_fit)

    convergence[b] <- (
      length(boot_fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages) > 0 ||
      !is.null(boot_fit@optinfo$conv$opt) &&
        boot_fit@optinfo$conv$opt != 0
    )
  }

  # Successful bootstrap replicates
  successful <- !failed

  valid_coefs <- boot_coefs[
    successful,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  # Percentile confidence intervals
  ci <- apply(
    valid_coefs,
    2,
    quantile,
    probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  results <- data.frame(
    term = terms,
    original_estimate = as.numeric(original_beta),
    bootstrap_mean = colMeans(valid_coefs),
    CI_lower = as.numeric(ci[1, ]),
    CI_upper = as.numeric(ci[2, ]),
    row.names = NULL
  )

  results$CI_excludes_zero <- (
    results$CI_lower > 0 |
    results$CI_upper < 0
  )

  list(
    results = results,
    diagnostics = data.frame(
      requested = B,
      successful = sum(successful),
      failed = sum(failed),
      singular_refits = sum(singular),
      convergence_warnings = sum(convergence)
    ),
    coefficients = valid_coefs
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Run the two selected models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

active_boot <- cluster_bootstrap(
  active_both_layers,
  B = 500,
  seed = 123
)

matching_boot <- cluster_bootstrap(
  matching_societal,
  B = 500,
  seed = 456
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------

active_boot$diagnostics
matching_boot$diagnostics

active_boot$results
matching_boot$results
```
